sanskrit: vyatītāyāṃ tu śarvaryām ādityasyodaye tataḥ sametya rājakartāraḥ sabhām īyur dvijātayaḥ
english: When that night had passed and the sun had risen, the royal ministers and the twice-born assembled together and proceeded to the council hall.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyo 'tha maudgalyo vāmadevaś ca kāśyapaḥ kātyayano gautamaś ca jābāliś ca mahāyaśāḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya, Maudgalya, Vāmadeva, Kāśyapa, Kātyāyana, Gautama, and the greatly renowned Jābāli —

sanskrit: ete dvijāḥ sahāmātyaiḥ pṛthag vācam udīrayan vasiṣṭham evābhimukhāḥ śreṣṭho rājapurohitam
english: these twice-born ones, together with the ministers, each raised their voice and turned to Vasiṣṭha, the foremost royal preceptor.

sanskrit: atītā śarvarī duḥkhaṃ yā no varṣaśatopamā asmin pañcatvam āpanne putraśokena pārthive
english: "That night has passed in grief — a night that seemed to us like a hundred years — now that this king has passed away into the five elements amid sorrow for his son."

sanskrit: svargataś ca mahārājo rāmaś cāraṇyam āśritaḥ lakṣmaṇaś cāpi tejasvī rāmeṇaiva gataḥ saha
english: "The great king has gone to heaven; Rāma has taken refuge in the forest; and the radiant Lakṣmaṇa has gone along with Rāma himself."

sanskrit: ubhau bharataśatrughnau kkekayeṣu paraṃtapau pure rājagṛhe ramye mātāmahaniveśane
english: "Both Bharata and Śatrughna, scorchers of foes, are in the Kekaya country, in the delightful city of Rājagṛha, in the residence of their maternal grandfather."

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇām ihādyaiva kaś cid rājā vidhīyatām arājakaṃ hi no rāṣṭraṃ na vināśam avāpnuyāt
english: "Let a king of the Ikṣvāku line be appointed here today. For a kingless realm of ours must not come to ruin."

sanskrit: nārājale janapade vidyunmālī mahāsvanaḥ abhivarṣati parjanyo mahīṃ divyena vāriṇā
english: In a kingless realm, the cloud-bearer garlanded with lightning and resounding with thunder does not shower the earth with divine waters.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade bījamuṣṭiḥ prakīryate nārākake pituḥ putro bhāryā vā vartate vaśe
english: In a kingless realm, no one sows a handful of seed; in a kingless realm, neither son nor wife remains under the father's authority.

sanskrit: arājake dhanaṃ nāsti nāsti bhāryāpy arājake idam atyāhitaṃ cānyat kutaḥ satyam arājake
english: Where there is no king, there is no wealth; where there is no king, there is no wife either. This and other extreme calamities arise — whence can truth exist where there is no king?

sanskrit: nārājake janapade kārayanti sabhāṃ narāḥ udyānāni ca ramyāṇi hṛṣṭāḥ puṇyagṛhāṇi ca
english: In a kingless realm, men do not build assembly halls, nor pleasant gardens, nor auspicious houses with joy.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade yajñaśīlā dvijātayaḥ satrāṇy anvāsate dāntā brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: In a kingless realm, the sacrifice-devoted twice-born do not attend soma-sessions; self-controlled brāhmaṇas with sharpened vows do not assemble.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade prabhūtanaṭanartakāḥ utsavāś ca samājāś ca vardhante rāṣṭravardhanāḥ
english: In a kingless realm, abundant actors and dancers do not flourish, nor do the festivals and fairs that cause the realm to prosper.

sanskrit: nārajake janapade siddhārthā vyavahāriṇaḥ kathābhir anurajyante kathāśīlāḥ kathāpriyaiḥ
english: In a kingless realm, those accomplished in affairs are not delighted by tales told by storytellers dear to the art of narration.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade vāhanaiḥ śīghragāmibhiḥ narā niryānty araṇyāni nārībhiḥ saha kāminaḥ
english: In a kingless realm, men do not venture forth into the forests with swift conveyances, accompanied by women, in the spirit of pleasure.

sanskrit: nārākaje janapade dhanavantaḥ surakṣitāḥ śerate vivṛta dvārāḥ kṛṣigorakṣajīvinaḥ
english: In a kingless realm, the wealthy do not sleep well-protected with open doors, nor do those who live by agriculture and cattle-herding.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade vaṇijo dūragāminaḥ gacchanti kṣemam adhvānaṃ bahupuṇyasamācitāḥ
english: In a kingless realm, merchants who travel far do not journey safely along the roads laden with abundant goods.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade caraty ekacaro vaśī bhāvayann ātmanātmānaṃ yatrasāyaṃgṛho muniḥ
english: In a kingless realm, the self-restrained sage who meditates upon himself through himself does not wander alone wherever he makes his evening abode.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade yogakṣemaṃ pravartate na cāpy arājake senā śatrūn viṣahate yudhi
english: In a kingless realm, welfare and security do not prevail; and in a kingless realm the army cannot withstand enemies in battle.

sanskrit: yathā hy anudakā nadyo yathā vāpy atṛṇaṃ vanam agopālā yathā gāvas tathā rāṣṭram arājakam
english: As rivers without water, as a forest without grass, as cows without a cowherd — so is a realm without a king.

sanskrit: nārājake janapade svakaṃ bhavati kasya cit matsyā iva narā nityaṃ bhakṣayanti parasparam
english: In a kingless realm, nothing belongs to anyone; men devour one another constantly like fish.

sanskrit: yehi saṃbhinnamaryādā nāstikāś chinnasaṃśayāḥ te 'pi bhāvāya kalpante rājadaṇḍanipīḍitāḥ
english: Even those who have broken all bounds, atheists devoid of doubt — even they are brought to proper conduct when constrained by the king's rod of punishment.

sanskrit: aho tama ivedaṃ syān na prajñāyeta kiṃ cana rājā cen na bhaveṃl loke vibhajan sādhvasādhunī
english: Alas, this world would be like darkness — nothing whatsoever would be discerned — if there were no king to distinguish the virtuous from the unvirtuous.

sanskrit: jīvaty api mahārāje tavaiva vacanaṃ vayam nātikramāmahe sarve velāṃ prāpyeva sāgaraḥ
english: "Even when the great king was alive, we all did not transgress your word, just as the ocean does not transgress its shore."

sanskrit: sa naḥ samīkṣya dvijavaryavṛttaṃ nṛpaṃ vinā rājyam araṇyabhūtam kumāram ikṣvākusutaṃ vadānyaṃ tvam eva rājānam ihābhiṣiñcaya
english: "Considering thus the conduct befitting the best of twice-born — the realm without a king become like a wilderness — do thou thyself consecrate here as king the generous prince, the son of the Ikṣvāku line."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha mitrāmātyagaṇān sarvān brāhmaṇāṃs tān idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having heard their words, Vasiṣṭha replied to all of them — the assembled allies, ministers, and those brāhmaṇas — with these words:

sanskrit: yad asau mātulakule pure rājagṛhe sukhī bharato vasati bhrātrā śatrughnena samanvitaḥ
english: "Since Bharata, accompanied by his brother Śatrughna, dwells happily in the city of Rājagṛha, the home of his maternal kinsmen —"

sanskrit: tac chīghraṃ javanā dūtā gacchantu tvaritair hayaiḥ ānetuṃ bhrātarau vīrau kiṃ samīkṣāmahe vayam
english: "— let swift messengers depart at once with fleet horses to bring back those two heroic brothers. Why should we hesitate?"

sanskrit: gacchantv iti tataḥ sarve vasiṣṭhaṃ vākyam abruvan teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vasiṣṭho vākyam abravīt
english: Then all of them said to Vasiṣṭha, "Let them go." Having heard their words, Vasiṣṭha spoke again:

sanskrit: ehi siddhārtha vijaya jayantāśokanandana śrūyatām itikartavyaṃ sarvān eva bravīmi vaḥ
english: "Come, Siddhārtha, Vijaya, Jayanta, Aśoka, Nandana — hear what is to be done. I speak to all of you."

sanskrit: puraṃ rājagṛhaṃ gatvā śīghraṃ śīghrajavair hayaiḥ tyaktaśokair idaṃ vācyaḥ śāsanād bharato mama
english: "Go quickly to the city of Rājagṛha with swift-galloping horses; by my command, let Bharata be told this, setting aside all grief:"

sanskrit: purohitas tvāṃ kuśalaṃ prāha sarve ca mantriṇaḥ tvaramāṇaś ca niryāhi kṛtyam ātyayikaḥ tvayā
english: "'The preceptor greets you well, as do all the ministers; depart in haste — there is an urgent matter requiring your action.'"

sanskrit: mā cāsmai proṣitaṃ rāmaṃ mā cāsmai pitaraṃ mṛtam bhavantaḥ śaṃsiṣur gatvā rāghavāṇām imaṃ kṣayam
english: "But do not tell him that Rāma has gone away, nor that his father has died; you must not announce to him this destruction of the Rāghava line."

sanskrit: kauśeyāni ca vastrāṇi bhūṣaṇāni varāṇi ca kṣipram ādāya rājñaś ca bharatasya ca gacchata vasiṣṭhenābhyanujñātā dūtāḥ saṃtvaritā yayuḥ
english: "Take quickly silk garments and choice ornaments for the king and for Bharata, and depart." Permitted by Vasiṣṭha, the messengers went forth in great haste.

sanskrit: te hastina pure gaṅgāṃ tīrtvā pratyaṅmukhā yayuḥ pāñcāladeśam āsādya madhyena kurujāṅgalam
english: They crossed the Gaṅgā at the city of Hastina and turned westward, reaching the Pāñcāla country and passing through the middle of the Kurujāṅgala.

sanskrit: te prasannodakāṃ divyāṃ nānāvihagasevitām upātijagmur vegena śaradaṇḍāṃ janākulām
english: With speed they passed the Śaradaṇḍā — a divine river of clear waters, frequented by many birds, and thronging with people.

sanskrit: nikūlavṛkṣam āsādya divyaṃ satyopayācanam abhigamyābhivādyaṃ taṃ kuliṅgāṃ prāviśan purīm
english: Reaching the Nikūla tree — that divine place of sacred vows — they approached and saluted it, then entered the city of Kuliṅgā.

sanskrit: abhikālaṃ tataḥ prāpya tejo'bhibhavanāc cyutāḥ yayur madhyena bāhlīkān sudāmānaṃ ca parvatam viṣṇoḥ padaṃ prekṣamāṇā vipāśāṃ cāpi śālmalīm
english: Then reaching the proper time, worn down by the exertion, they passed through the Bāhlīka country and the mountain Sudāmā, gazing upon Viṣṇu's footprint, and also the Vipāśā river and the Śālmalī tree.

sanskrit: te śrāntavāhanā dūtā vikṛṣṭena satā pathā giri vrajaṃ pura varaṃ śīghram āsedur añjasā
english: Those messengers, with their mounts weary, traveling along a long and good road, swiftly and straightway reached Girivraja, that excellent city.

sanskrit: bhartuḥ priyārthaṃ kularakṣaṇārthaṃ bhartuś ca vaṃśasya parigrahārtham aheḍamānās tvarayā sma dūtā rātryāṃ tu te tat puram eva yātāḥ
english: For the sake of pleasing their lord, for the protection of the lineage, and for the sustaining of their master's dynasty — without any hesitation, those messengers hastened and arrived at that very city in the night.

sanskrit: yām eva rātriṃ te dūtāḥ praviśanti sma tāṃ purīm bharatenāpi tāṃ rātriṃ svapno dṛṣṭo 'yam apriyaḥ
english: On the very same night that those messengers entered the city, Bharata too saw this ill-omened dream.

sanskrit: vyuṣṭām eva tu tāṃ rātriṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ svapnam apriyam putro rājādhirājasya subhṛśaṃ paryatapyata
english: When that night was over and he had seen that inauspicious dream, the son of the king of kings was deeply tormented.

sanskrit: tapyamānaṃ samājñāya vayasyāḥ priyavādinaḥ āyāsaṃ hi vineṣyantaḥ sabhāyāṃ cakrire kathāḥ
english: Perceiving him to be distressed, his friends, who spoke pleasant words, began telling tales in the assembly-hall, intending thereby to drive away his suffering.

sanskrit: vādayanti tathā śāntiṃ lāsayanty api cāpare nāṭakāny apare prāhur hāsyāni vividhāni ca
english: Some played musical instruments to soothe him; others danced; yet others performed plays and various comic entertainments.

sanskrit: sa tair mahātmā bharataḥ sakhibhiḥ priya vādibhiḥ goṣṭhīhāsyāni kurvadbhir na prāhṛṣyata rāghavaḥ
english: Yet that great-souled Bharata, that Rāghava, did not rejoice with those friends who spoke kindly to him and who made merry with tales and laughter.

sanskrit: tam abravīt priyasakho bharataṃ sakhibhir vṛtam suhṛdbhiḥ paryupāsīnaḥ kiṃ sakhe nānumodase
english: His dear friend, attended by companions and surrounded by well-wishers, said to Bharata: "Why, friend, do you not take delight?"

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ suhṛdaṃ bharataḥ pratyuvāca ha śṛṇu tvaṃ yan nimittaṃme dainyam etad upāgatam
english: To his friend speaking thus, Bharata replied: "Hear what is the cause of this despondency that has come upon me."

sanskrit: svapne pitaram adrākṣaṃ malinaṃ muktamūrdhajam patantam adriśikharāt kaluṣe gomaye hrade
english: "In a dream I saw my father, begrimed and with hair unbound, falling from a mountain peak into a turbid lake of cow-dung."

sanskrit: plavamānaś ca me dṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmin gomayahrade pibann añjalinā tailaṃ hasann iva muhur muhuḥ
english: "And I saw him wallowing in that lake of cow-dung, drinking oil with cupped hands, laughing as it were again and again."

sanskrit: tatas tilodanaṃ bhuktvā punaḥ punar adhaḥśirāḥ tailenābhyaktasarvāṅgas tailam evāvagāhata
english: "Then, having eaten sesame-rice, again and again with his head downward, his whole body anointed with oil, he plunged into the oil itself."

sanskrit: svapne 'pi sāgaraṃ śuṣkaṃ candraṃ ca patitaṃ bhuvi sahasā cāpi saṃśantaṃ jvalitaṃ jātavedasaṃ
english: "In the dream I also saw the ocean dried up, the moon fallen suddenly to the earth, and the sacrificial fire extinguished all at once."

sanskrit: avadīrṇāṃ ca pṛthivīṃ śuṣkāṃś ca vividhān drumān ahaṃ paśyāmi vidhvastān sadhūmāṃś caiva pārvatān
english: "I see the earth rent asunder, various trees withered and shattered, and the mountains smoking."

sanskrit: pīṭhe kārṣṇāyase cainaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ kṛṣṇavāsasaṃ prahasanti sma rājānaṃ pramadāḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalāḥ
english: "I saw the king seated on an iron throne, dressed in black garments, while dark-tawny women laughed and mocked at him."

sanskrit: tvaramāṇaś ca dharmātmā raktamālyānulepanaḥ rathena kharayuktena prayāto dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ
english: "And that righteous-souled one, adorned with red garlands and red unguents, was hastening away on a chariot yoked with donkeys, heading southward."

sanskrit: evam etan mayā dṛṣṭam imāṃ rātriṃ bhayāvahām ahaṃ rāmo 'tha vā rājā lakṣmaṇo vā mariṣyati
english: "Thus have I seen this terror-inducing vision this night. Either Rāma, or the king, or Lakṣmaṇa will die."

sanskrit: naro yānena yaḥ svapne kharayuktena yāti hi acirāt tasya dhūmāgraṃ citāyāṃ saṃpradṛśyate etannimittaṃ dīno 'haṃ tan na vaḥ pratipūjaye
english: "For the man who in a dream travels in a conveyance yoked with donkeys — before long the smoke of his funeral pyre is seen rising. It is for this reason that I am wretched; therefore I cannot respond to your cheer."

sanskrit: śuṣyatīva ca me kaṇṭho na svastham iva me manaḥ jugupsann iva cātmānaṃ na ca paśyāmi kāraṇam
english: "My throat seems to dry up; my mind is as though unsettled; I seem to shudder within myself — yet I see no cause for it."

sanskrit: imāṃ hi duḥsvapnagatiṃ niśāmya tām anekarūpām avitarkitāṃ purā bhayaṃ mahat tad dhṛdayān na yāti me vicintya rājānam acintyadarśanam
english: "Having witnessed this course of evil dreams — so manifold, so unforeseen — that great fear does not leave my heart, as I reflect upon the king whose sight is beyond imagining."
